recipe.class: LowLatency with DSpark (the one scored class)
recipe.startup_max_wait_note: equal to infb.efficiency.deadlines.launch_s. serve.py hands it to upstream's RemoteOpenAIServer as max_wait_seconds, for the session's launch and the relaunch's second launch. The alarm at launch_s is armed when the first node's set-up starts, before the server wrapper's own wait begins, so a first launch that runs out of launch_s ends by that alarm, whose message the slow-host rule reads (tests/infb_verify/slow_host.py); a wait shorter than launch_s would end it first, with the wrapper's own error, and the rule would never apply

session.note: launch 7000 + measurement 1150 (decode_c1 650: five draws; throughput 500: three draws and the canary) + GSM8K 60 + fidelity 180 (a re-send per sequence and a re-draw per band at most) + served configuration 60 + the relaunch 16430 (both sides' second launches, run within the verifier's clock) + the two scored nodes at node_default_s 60 each (they judge from the record) + teardown 180 + a margin of 60 (the session's own time beyond its nodes' measured 0.6 s at most)

gsm8k_floor_record.rule: floor(mean - 3 x SE) questions of 200, SE = the run-to-run sample sd over the clean oracle launches, floored at one question
launches: an earlier served session of an earlier recipe
gsm8k_floor_record.note: the five clean launches of the closure oracle (each on its own port, health from its own server log); the within-launch repeats are two more runs on the same server after its efficiency draws, recorded apart

fidelity_T_record.rule: max(0.05, 3 x the largest per-band median over the clean oracle launches)
launches: an earlier served session of an earlier recipe
fidelity_T_record.superseded: one T (0.13665) for the worst band became a bar per band, fidelity_T_per_band

fidelity_T_per_band_record.rule: T_b = max(floor_b, k_b x f_b); f_b the median of the recorded oracle draws for band b over three independent oracle runs; k_b = 3 on every band (with the three-quarter rule: no quality control passes a band at 3x and fails it at 2x); floor_b = 0.05 on every band (above every cross-configuration threshold upstream uses). The verdict is the conjunction over bands. A sequence over its T_b is re-sent once and keeps the lower reading; a band over its T_b is re-drawn once whole and fails only if both draws are over.
fidelity_T_per_band_record.false_fail_model: per band, a normal model of the band median over every recorded oracle draw; two draws independent

rederived.rule: f_b re-derived from at least six current-verifier oracle draws, T_b = max(0.05, 3 x f_b) as set; the table moves by arithmetic only where a bar moves at five decimals

efficiency.kit: the task's own efficiency implementation (tests/infb_efficiency), customized and owned by the task; provenance in tests/infb_efficiency/PROVENANCE.json and tests/_upstream/PROVENANCE.md
efficiency.c1_attempts_note: 1: decode_c1_draws takes the median of five draws on both sides, and the candidate-only attempts retire with it (the implementation refuses c1_attempts above 1 beside it). This recipe's per-request decode speed at concurrency 1 is bimodal under DSpark (a measurement: 218-278 and 385-438 tok/s); the median of per-prompt ratios and the median of five draws on both sides carry that

sparse_build.note: the reference snapshot fix: the pristine image's sparse runtime products are the unimplemented runtime's, so they are never copied into the reference (build_product_exclude); snapshot.py runs the narrow builder on the restored reference tree with the engine's interpreter and records every product it writes, which reference.py re-hashes at grading time; source_id is the builder's id of the restored source

test_hidden.C_rule_row: a low-latency recipe: C = 16. The scored class is LowLatency with DSpark.

launch.why_static: no registered upstream class launches this recipe (the maintainers' obligations here are unit tests and a plain evaluator), so the argv is given, and infb_verify/test_hidden.py asserts at import that it equals the recipe the candidate is launched with (config.json infb.recipe)

test_hidden.host_checks_note: none: upstream asserts no speed, throughput or acceptance threshold for this model at the landing

deadlines.status: composed from the measured per-axis draw durations and the common invocation limit
deadlines.launch_rule: the public startup limit (spawn through the ready health response)
deadlines.relaunch_note: the relaunch node holds the reference's second launch, its two axis invocations and its teardown, then the candidate's stop, second launch, check and two axis invocations, each operation at its public limit
deadlines.invocation_note: an axis's prescribed draws on either side are one measurement invocation under the public one-invocation limit, 1,800 s, dispatch through every draw's record; each draw receives what remains of it.

efficiency.relaunch_note: an axis is relaunched on both sides when its ratio lies in [0.8 x (1 - m), 0.8 / (1 - b)) or the reference's kept value is below (1 - b) of the recipe's figure. b 0.18 and m 0.15 are the values this task runs with. The reference figures are decode_c1 300 tok/s (the band at 246) and throughput 1,569.75 tok/s, the median of the reference's kept throughput over the recorded reference runs (the band at 1,287); every healthy reference recorded is above both bands. order 'session': the server fixture is session-scoped and shared with test_fidelity.py, so the relaunch runs after every node the first launch serves. prior_reports: L0 runs before this session, and a graded L0 id that failed or was skipped makes the reward 0 whatever the efficiency nodes say. The relaunch runs within the time the verifier's clock leaves (infb.verifier_clock), or is skipped with a re-run request

sizing.measured: the slowest draw recorded on an oracle tree on either side, slowed windows included: decode_c1 39.22 s (the reference; 30.91 s on healthy hosts), throughput 47.33 s (the candidate; 34.70 s on healthy hosts); the client's start about 2 s (node call less attempt, 1.6-1.8 s); a canary reading 11.17 s at most

infb._diagnostic_node_ids_note: the efficiency gate's measurement and relaunch nodes, recorded and not scored.

verifier_clock.note: cap_s is task.toml's [verifier] timeout_sec; before_s is what the cap spends before test.sh's first line, the verifier environment's build bound and 300 s to start it (measured: 8-12 s with a warm build cache, 1,201-1,494 s with a tail-only build); tail_s is what test.sh runs after its last bounded group (measured at most 63.1 s; 200, 3 x that rounded up). The build bound inside before_s is enforced on Modal and Daytona only; on Docker the cap alone bounds the verifier build, so there before_s is an allowance, 2.6x the slowest start measured (1,494 s). A start past it leaves END_BY later by as much, so a relaunch that runs to END_BY can meet the cap: a verifier timeout, never a verdict.

preflight.note: preflight bounded as a group, at 3 x its measured worst (43.9 s) rounded up; an overrun exits 3 (no reward, the -1 sentinel), as a failed preflight does, so a 10 s kill-after suffices

reference_phase.note: the reference phase bounded as one group, at 3 x its measured worst on the grading hosts (a 2,330.3 s launch plus a non-launch part of 305 s at most with slowed draws, 2,635 s) rounded up; it also holds one crash and the retry inside launch_s. An overrun exits 3 (a host fault, the -1 sentinel), as a reference failure does

l0.note: L0 bounded as a group, at 3 x its measured worst with the advertised rebuild, rounded up to 10 s. The worst is the sizing control on a grading host: L0 1,624.1 s, of which the task's build.sh after a one-line .cu change took 1,495.2 s, a full compile every time (the build's temp directory is random, so the image's ccache never hits: 0 of 419, where the same rebuild took 1,396 s at the verifier's limits, 64 CPUs and 512 GB). The rebuild's own bound (INFB_REBUILD_TIMEOUT_SEC, test.sh sets it from rebuild_timeout_s) sits 300 s inside the group's, 3.06 x that rebuild, so a rebuild that overruns fails inside pytest with its reason in junit; the 60 s kill-after lets the compile's process group end before the session starts. The group's fifth node, test_registered_class_constructs, is one runtime observation under the public 1,800 s limit, so its bound is composed as max(3R, 1,800 + 60) = 1,860 s (R measured on the reference), and the group's bound is the five nodes' bounds plus the 60 s dispatch allowance: 7,640 s

construct.cap_note: the node's own bound B, which test_l0.py enforces instead of the common invocation cap, because one runtime observation of this node is longer than one unit-test file process. The rule, fixed before any reading: B = max(3 x the reference's largest measured wall, invocation + kill_after_s = 1,860 s), from three runs of the reference, each alone on its host. Each rank's peak host RSS is recorded beside its wall and is never graded
construct.note: tests/infb_verify/construct.py builds the engine's configuration from the served command line (the recipe's grading copy: the model, the recipe's arguments and --seed 0) and runs one process per rank of it (TP 4): the engine's worker distributed initialisation, the model built as the engine's loader builds it (initialize_model under the model's default dtype on the rank's device), and then the constructed class's own load_weights, called once over a lazy generator that walks the checkpoint shard by shard in the index's order and creates each tensor only when the loader draws it, with the exact name, dtype and shape from that shard's safetensors header. No tensor data is read and no shard is memory-mapped. Each tensor is backed by its own untouched private anonymous mapping of exactly its nbytes, wrapped with torch.frombuffer and reinterpreted: the node must not change what the class under test does, and what it does may be to hold every tensor at once (the reference's own load_weights sorts the whole iterable before it copies anything, and a candidate's may too), so the tensors are made cheap to hold instead. Untouched anonymous pages read as zeros from the kernel's shared zero page, so holding the checkpoint costs address space, not memory; the mapping is contiguous and page-aligned, so every dtype reinterpretation a loader may do still works, and it is never written to. Every name the index holds passes exactly once, checked as it goes and again at the end. Structural and deterministic: no tolerance. records: every rank's record and the node's (construct.json), and the program's output (construct.log). grace_s: after a rank fails, how long the others may run before they are stopped (they wait on it in a collective). release_wait_s: how long the node waits for the GPUs to be free after it, before step 3a's own check

materials.note: the evaluation materials, one commit after the kernel-prepared base, made by both Dockerfiles with a pinned identity and date and asserted there as MATERIALS_HEAD_SHA. It is the agent's starting HEAD and the base the submission is taken from (pre_artifacts.sh), the grader's resets and the oracle's.
materials.starting_head_note: the agent's starting HEAD is the sparse-indexer preparation commit atop this one (infb.sparse_preparation); this commit and its assertion in both Dockerfiles are unchanged

preservation.note: the existing-engine tests at the prepared base, unmodified -- every base instance of every named function that exists at base, less the instances excluded by record. Each file runs in its own pytest process from /app with the rootdir at /app, only its listed ids; tests/eval/deepseek_v41_flash/tests/selection.json is the same list for the agent.
preservation.budget_note: the public operation limit for one existing-engine unit-test file process (1,800 s: collection and every selected case in the file, including compilation); a file over it on a healthy host fails
preservation.selection_map: the recorded instance-level selection: base x3 and reference x3 qualification runs in the task image

unrelated_request.prompt: Here is a short list of prime numbers: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11,

history.note: each mode's median over the four records against the 20,480 band's existing T; self_consistency takes the server's teacher-forced rescoring of its own 512 generated tokens as the reference and the emitted decode log-probabilities as the candidate

chat.note: framing, stream assembly, the second turn carrying the first, requested-token log-probabilities, and each concurrent teacher-forced reading within its band's existing fidelity allowance of its solo reading (mean k3, solo as the reference)

_old_l2_record.note: a block of landing test files and the initialization test; not read by the verifier

runtime_evidence.note: applied to this recipe: an instrumented launch of the recipe plus the engine's own torch-profiler configuration, in its own group after the timed session; warm C1 and C16 workloads at 4,096/512 drawn from the private pool with the efficiency client's draw_workload; per observed interval, CUDA-graph replay of model kernels on all four ranks, draft work and at least one accepted draft token from the engine's counters, the generated-token counter equal to the tokens returned; the two observed inputs' generations distinct and, as a median of their mean k3 against the server's own rescoring, at most the 20,480 band's existing bar (the history test's self-consistency statistic and bar)

sparse_preparation.note: the agent's starting HEAD, the base of the submission (pre_artifacts.sh), of the grader's resets and of the oracle; asserted by both Dockerfiles' step 14; its content manifest is environment/sparse-indexer/preparation.lock.json (and the verifier's copy)

sparse_indexer.note: the private configuration of the seven sparse-indexer nodes. The public protocol constants live in the materials' sparse_indexer/ (measure.py, contract.py, reference.py) and must equal the ones here; the seeds, the case ids, the workload matrix and the bounds are private.

canary.note: the task's existing tolerances and attribution: readings before and after each role's component phase; an unhealthy reading voids the component nodes, it never triggers a redraw

operation_caps_s.note: the public operation limits these processes are enforced at: a component phase's warm work within the rebuild cap (4,580 s) and its measurement within the invocation cap (1,800 s); a corpus family's process within the unit-file cap (1,800 s); the binding node's probe requests within the HTTP cap (900 s each)

sparse_indexer.case_ids_note: the weight-rounding requirement is observed on production tensors in test_sparse_indexer_serving_binding, not by a direct fused-query case in the packed family (tests import no future helper name); 41 cases in four families

group_bounds.note: components_s bounds test.sh's component group; the reference's two component phases are inside reference_phase.budget_s and the binding node inside runtime_evidence.group_budget_s (the shared launch counted once)
